description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs (4 additional sync hooks)

JMAP-x2gd.43 ('ChatBackend::limits is sync') states in its
description:

  > The trait's other hooks (slow_mode_check, is_contact_blocked,
  > may_set_custom_emoji, expire_message, apply_space_patch,
  > apply_space_metadata_patch) are all async. limits is the odd
  > one out.

That enumeration is incorrect. FOUR other ChatBackend methods are
sync:

1. supports_type<O: JmapObject>(&self) -> bool         (line 282)
2. generate_invite_code(&self) -> String                (line 310)
3. protect_last_admin(&self, caller, account_id) -> bool (line 517)
4. retains_edit_history(&self) -> bool                  (line 559)

All four share the same contract risk that JMAP-x2gd.43 identifies
for limits():

- Production backends that need to consult per-tenant DB / cache /
  external policy service for the answer must block_on() or
  block_in_place() inside the sync method. Both are runtime-pinning
  hazards in a Send context.
- Once the trait ships sync, flipping to async is a major-version
  break. Backend implementors who built the sync shape are stuck.

Per-method analysis:

1. supports_type — covered separately in JMAP-x2gd.46 (the args
   gap is the more pressing issue there; sync-ness compounds it).
   A multi-tenant backend that wants 'Pro tier exposes
   CustomEmoji' has to lazy-load and cache from a DB at startup
   if forced sync.

2. generate_invite_code — JMAP-x2gd.36 covers the length /
   charset / fallibility contract, but not sync-ness. A backend
   using an HSM-backed entropy source (security-critical
   deployments use this) or one that needs to check the
   generated code against an existing-codes table to dedupe
   cannot do that async from this method.

3. protect_last_admin — production backends may want to consult
   the deployment's admin-tracking store (a separate
   service-level identity backend). Sync rules that out.

4. retains_edit_history — the doc-comment on this method
   (lines 543-561) explicitly addresses the limitation: 'This is
   a static deployment-policy flag, not a per-call decision …
   Production backends that need to vary retention per-account
   would file a follow-up bead for a parallel
   retains_edit_history_for_account hook rather than reshaping
   this method.'
   This admits the current shape cannot grow, and announces that
   the fix will be an asymmetric parallel method. That is a
   contract-level acknowledgement that the sync no-args shape is
   wrong for multi-tenant production deployments.

Pattern conclusion: the workspace has FIVE sync hooks
(limits + the four above) plus FIVE async hooks (slow_mode_check,
is_contact_blocked, may_set_custom_emoji, expire_message,
apply_space_patch / apply_space_metadata_patch). The async hooks
are the ones consumed on the hot mutation path; the sync hooks
are the policy / capability hooks. That carve-up is plausible
but the workspace did not document it.

Recommended fix (matching JMAP-x2gd.43's recommendation): convert
all five policy hooks to async with default impls that simply
return the current sync value. Or: explicitly document the
sync-by-design carve-up so future contributors know not to
'fix' it by making them all async.

This finding does NOT depend on JMAP-x2gd.43 being closed first;
it's a correction to the enumeration of sync methods in the .43
description and a scope expansion of the same complaint to four
more sites.
title: API contract: four other ChatBackend methods are sync alongside limits (JMAP-x2gd.43 enumeration was wrong)
